answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every identity to post a refundable stake bond before earning rewards, with trust growing only through verifiable completed work. Like a falcon proving its skill before joining the flock, a new agent starts with little weight. A willow-like reputation graph then exposes fake clusters, since Sybils share funders, timing, and counterparties, letting peers discount them as one entity. Rewards flow like an ocean current toward proven contributors, not identity count, so spinning up shells costs more in bonds than it can repay.
